anode_vs_cathode_summary._definition: side = which interface the product passivates. anode = reduction front V->0 (Li metal contact); cathode = oxidation front V>=2.45 V; bulk-GB = grain-boundary electron network always present.

anode_side_V_to_0.benefit: O-derived Li2O (and bulk/GB Li3PO4 5.73) provide a wide-gap, electronically insulating film that REPLACES the conductive Li3P (0.70 eV) that the undoped cell forms against Li metal. Blocks e- leak -> suppresses internal Li0 plating / dendrite / self-discharge (Han 2019).
anode_side_V_to_0.Nd_role: negative at the anode: Nd is reduced to conductive NdP -> Nd itself does NOT help the anode; the anode benefit is the O effect (Li2O/Li3PO4), not Nd.

cathode_side_V_ge_2.45.benefit: Nd3+ survives the oxidizing potential (Nd4+ inaccessible) and anchors O into wide-gap NdPO4 / NdCl3 / Li3PO4 passivation, versus modelc's CONDUCTIVE polysulfide/chloride decomposition products. This is where Nd's niche actually is (high-V cathode passivation), not ionic conductivity.
cathode_side_V_ge_2.45.Nd_role: positive at the cathode: Nd3+ is the high-V anchor that keeps O/Cl in wide-gap form.

direct_convex_hull_staircase_2026_06_24._what: Intrinsic grand-potential ESW staircase for the Nd-doped composition itself (esw_grand_potential.py, 6-element Cl-Li-Nd-O-P-S hull). Moves the anode/cathode SEI story from INFERENCE (product gaps + bulk-opposite logic) to DIRECT proof: the convex hull is asked, at each voltage, what the doped cell decomposes into. Full log: tools/oxidation/esw_nd_result.txt ; data: db/properties/oxidation_stability.json (nd_doped).
direct_convex_hull_staircase_2026_06_24._control: modelc re-run on the SAME 6-element hull reproduces the 4-element-hull modelc breakpoint-for-breakpoint -> the nd-vs-modelc product divergence is REAL chemistry, not a hull artifact.

CONFIRMED.anode_V0: O -> 0.3 Li2O (5.24) at the Li-metal contact.
CONFIRMED.cathode_highV: NdPO4 (5.55) @2.45 V ; NdCl3 (4.30) @2.62 V ; LiNd(PO3)4 @3.08 V ; Nd(PO3)3 @3.66 V -- all wide-gap; modelc gives only conductive P2S7/LiS4/S/SCl/PCl5.
CONFIRMED.Nd_split: Nd -> NdP/Nd2S3 (conductive) at low V [anode-bad]; Nd -> NdPO4/NdCl3 (wide-gap) only at high V [cathode-good] -- the anode/cathode split is confirmed by the actual reactions.

CORRECTIONS.intrinsic_window_NARROWS: nd ESW = 0.40 V (1.52-1.92) vs modelc 0.90 V (1.24-2.14). Nd-S/Nd-P/Nd-O redox is active inside modelc's window -> nd is intrinsically LESS stable, not more. Benefit is product electron-blocking (kinetic passivation), NOT a wider thermodynamic window (parallel to the bulk-gap narrowing).
CORRECTIONS.O_too_dilute_at_x0.2: V=0 gives 0.3 Li2O + 0.8 Li3P -> O does NOT fully replace conductive Li3P; the wide-gap conversion is PARTIAL/ADDITIVE and scales with O (a GB/interphase percolation-breaking effect, not bulk replacement). Softens the earlier 'Li2O replaces Li3P' phrasing.
CORRECTIONS.polysulfides_remain: nd ADDS NdPO4/NdCl3/Li3PO4 alongside P2S7/SCl/PCl5 (which still form); it does not eliminate them. NdPO4 first appears at 2.45 V, so passivation is a >=2.45 V (cathode operating) effect; 1.92-2.45 V oxidizes to non-wide-gap Nd-sulfides.

oxophilicity_descriptor_eV_per_anion._definition: oxophilicity(M) = Ef/anion(M-sulfide) - Ef/anion(M-oxide); larger = stronger O getter.
oxophilicity_descriptor_eV_per_anion._reading: Nd (1.75) ~= Li (1.67) -> Nd is NOT a special O-getter. The benefit of incorporated O is an O effect, not an Nd effect; Nd is just an O carrier.

formation_and_thermodynamics._why_this_matters: Formation/stability energies explain WHY the wide-gap O/Nd products form preferentially (product SELECTION), while interface reactivity gives the decomposition AMOUNT (similar doped vs undoped).
formation_and_thermodynamics.Nd2O3_note: one of the most thermodynamically stable lanthanide oxides -> O is strongly locked as oxide/phosphate, does not release; favors Nd-O / P-O over Nd-S (Nd2S3 less stable). Source: modelc_nd_doped.json.
formation_and_thermodynamics.O_at_PS4_note: Track 1A (O substituting a PS4 corner S -> phosphate-like PS3O/PS2O2) is 0.67 eV/O more stable than O at a free 4d site; AIMD shows spontaneous P-O formation at 500 K. -> O preferentially builds the wide-gap phosphate precursor inside the host. Source: modelc_nd_doped.json.
formation_and_thermodynamics.ICOHP_P_O_note: P-O is the strongest host bond (+41% vs P-S -5.98) -> O is bonding-locked; reinforces that O stays incorporated and forms phosphate. Source: db/properties/nd_icohp.json.

interface_reactivity_vs_cathode.OCV_reading: nd (-0.3285) ~= modelc (-0.3308): the decomposition AMOUNT is essentially the same (only 0.0023 eV/atom less negative). Doping does NOT reduce how much reacts -> the benefit is that the PRODUCTS become wide-gap (electron-blocking), not that less reacts. comp1 least reactive.
interface_reactivity_vs_cathode.OCV_products: all -> Co9S8 + Li3PO4 + Li2S + LiCl + Li2SO4 (phosphate O comes from the cathode, so Li3PO4 CEI forms regardless of doping); nd additionally forms Nd2SO2.
interface_reactivity_vs_cathode.voltage_resolved_v2_note: Charged-state (operating V) GrandPotentialInterfacialReactivity: both SEs react more strongly with V (-0.6 -> -1.6 eV/atom @4.3 V); Cl-rich (LPSCl1.6) thermodynamically LESS reactive than LPSCl at every V. The Nd cycling benefit is therefore NOT a smaller cathode reaction -> it is the electron-blocking product set. See kb/results/interface_reactivity_v2_voltage_resolved_2026_06_21.md.

caveats: Nd-bearing MP gaps are LOWER BOUNDS (4f mis-placement); pure-O phases (Li3PO4 5.73, Li2O 5.24, LiCl 6.65) are reliable -> the O message is independent of Nd-4f uncertainty.

Roles/sides and the GB electron-blocking mechanism are an INFERENCE from product gaps + the bulk-opposite-direction logic; GB/interface electron transport and SEI morphology were NOT computed directly -> needs XPS depth / ToF-SIMS / SSRM validation.
Interface reactivity is thermodynamic (zero/grand-potential), kinetic CEI passivation not captured; LiCoO2 proxy (experiment may use NCM).
DFT doping x=0.2 (10x the experimental x=0.02) -> trends/mechanism robust, absolute values approximate.
